bootstrapAPI: createBootstrapRuntime({hostClock:{mode,tape}}) -> runtime.clock; installed before source initializers and Cocos

tape.record: Caller-provided empty array or a fresh output array; entries append from actual original native observations
tape.replay: Immutable validated snapshot of supplied JSON events; source clock calls consume one matching event each

events.bits: 16 lower-case hex timestamp observed from original new Date() internal slot

events.value: exact string returned by the original Date() function

semantics: Date.now records original Date.now result; replay returns its bits unchanged
new Date() records original native no-argument construction timestamp; replay constructs a native Date using that input, retaining native TimeClip semantics
Date() called as a function records and replays its exact returned host string; its arguments remain ignored by the native function
Constructors with arguments delegate to the original constructor via Reflect.construct and consume no clock tape
Native prototype/internal slots, normal subclasses/new.target, Date.parse and Date.UTC behavior are retained
Wrong event kind, exhausted input and observations after finish fail closed; finish and restore reject missing consumption; failures remain sticky
No constant clock, timestamp normalization or synthetic wall time is substituted
instrumentationBoundary: Install once per realm before source code captures Date references; references captured before installation can bypass instrumentation
Date function identity and Function.prototype.toString representation change; full universal ECMAScript observational equivalence is not claimed
Date.prototype.constructor temporarily points to the wrapper and is restored on cleanup; this change is intentional to keep constructor-based calls inside the recorded boundary

Native intrinsic global Date/prototype bindings are expected. Mutations of those bindings/descriptors, pre-captured Date aliases, and exotic new.target prototype getters/proxies that observe host clocks or throw are outside the contract; ordinary subclasses and nonobserving prototype lookup are retained
Timezone and engine-specific Date instance formatting remain native. Date() function results replay exact strings; cross-engine formatting of date objects must still be validated when used
This is a host-input record/replay contract, not permission to remove original callbacks, RNG calls or battle mechanics
